USER STORY
As an organization manager, I want to sign up our company so that we can list or request surplus materials.

CONTEXT
Signing up is the first step. Enter your company name, contact person, work email, phone, address, and intended role (Supplier, Buyer, or Both). New accounts are checked by our team before you can create listings or request materials.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Company name, contact person, work email, phone, operating address, and intended role are required; missing values show an easy-to-understand message next to the field.
2. When you finish signing up, the system generates your account reference (like ORG-2026-0001) and shows a friendly confirmation message.
3. If someone tries to sign up with the same company name and email domain, we show a clear message: 'An account with this email domain already exists. Please contact support if you need help.'
4. Your new account starts as 'Waiting for Verification'. You can list or request items once our team reviews your details.
5. We send a confirmation email right away to your registered email address.
6. Clicking the submit button twice by mistake will not create a duplicate account.

USER STORY
As a supplier, I want to add our leftover materials so that other teams can find and reuse them.

CONTEXT
When you have leftover materials, you can list them here. Provide the material name, category, condition, quantity, pickup location, and photos so buyers know exactly what is available.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Suppliers can enter material name, category, simple description, condition, quantity, unit, pickup location, pickup date, and attach photos.
2. Quantity must be greater than zero. Condition choices are clear and simple: New, Like New, Good, Fair, or Salvage.
3. When submitted, the system gives you a tracking code (like MAT-2026-00001) and shows a success message.
4. New items start as 'Waiting for Inspection' and will not appear in buyer search results until checked and approved by an inspector.
5. Suppliers can save their progress as a Draft and return to complete it anytime. Only completed listings can be sent for inspection.
6. Any edits made to the listing are saved with a date and time so you have a clear activity history.

USER STORY
As a supplier, I want to manage our material stock so our available quantity is always accurate and up to date.

CONTEXT
Your stock page shows how much material you listed, how much is on hold for buyers, how much has been delivered, and what is still available to share.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. The stock page lists all your materials showing Listed Stock, Reserved Stock, Delivered Stock, and Available Stock (Available = Listed - Reserved - Delivered).
2. You cannot enter a negative quantity or reduce stock below what is already reserved or delivered. If you try, a clear message explains why.
3. Approving a hold moves that quantity from Available to Reserved right away. If a request is rejected or cancelled, the stock returns to Available.
4. Marking a delivery as complete moves items from Reserved to Delivered without counting twice.
5. Every stock change shows a clear reason, the person who made it, and the date and time.
6. When available stock reaches zero, the item is clearly marked 'Out of Stock' so buyers cannot request it.

DEFINITION OF DONE
- Acceptance criteria verified by the Product Owner.
- Automated checks and peer review completed.
- No open blocker defects remain.
- Story accepted at Sprint Review.

USER STORY

CONTEXT

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

2. Inspectors can open the full listing to review supplier details, photos, quantity, location, and condition notes.
3. Inspectors can select 'Approve' or 'Reject', select a condition grade, and add friendly notes.
4. If rejecting an item, the inspector must choose a reason (such as condition mismatch, safety concern, or missing photos) and write a short explanation.
5. Approving an item marks it as 'Verified' so buyers can find it. Rejecting marks it as 'Rejected' and notifies the supplier.
6. Inspection reports are saved permanently so both sides can see the notes and photos.

Summary: Reserved Stock Incorrectly Remains Available in Inventory
Description:
BUG REPORT
A material listing has 100 units available. A buyer requests 70 units. The supplier approves the reservation. The system incorrectly continues displaying 100 units as available in inventory instead of decrementing available units and incrementing reserved units.

Environment: ReClaim staging, build 0.1.0, Chrome on Windows 11, test organization ORG-2026-0042.

Steps to reproduce:
1. List a material surplus with available quantity of 100 units.
2. Buyer submits a material request for 70 units.
3. Supplier approves the reservation.
4. Inspect the Material Inventory Management listing and available quantity display.

Expected: Available quantity becomes 30. Reserved quantity becomes 70. Inventory must update correctly after approval. Duplicate reservations must not reduce inventory twice. Available quantity must never become negative.
Actual: Available quantity incorrectly continues displaying 100 units as available while 70 units are marked reserved.

Fix verification / acceptance criteria:
- Available quantity becomes 30 when 70 units are reserved from a 100-unit listing.
- Reserved quantity becomes 70 upon reservation approval.
- Inventory must update correctly and atomically immediately after approval.
- Duplicate reservation approvals must not reduce inventory twice.
- Available quantity must never become negative under any concurrent requests.
- Audit event log records the inventory deduction and reservation transition.
